Purpose
This document explains the two core halves of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system. Phase A prepares a
knowledge file for search. Phase B accepts a user's question, finds the most relevant stored information, sends that
context to an API-based LLM, and prints the answer.

Important idea
The LLM does not normally search your document itself. The application performs retrieval first. The LLM receives the
selected context and generates a natural-language answer from it.
PHASE A — INDEXING A FILE
1. Read a File of Any Type
There is no single Python function that can meaningfully read every file type. First identify the file type, then use an
appropriate parser/loader. Examples include TXT, PDF, DOCX, CSV, XLSX, PPTX, HTML, and JSON.

Why metadata matters
Metadata lets you later identify the source document and page. It can also support filtering by document, department,
customer, or authorized scope.
2. Extract Text
Examples of Python libraries commonly used for RAG document extraction include PyMuPDF or pypdf for PDF,
python-docx for DOCX, pandas/openpyxl for tabular files, python-pptx for PowerPoint, BeautifulSoup for HTML, and

Python's built-in json module for JSON. RAG frameworks can also provide loaders around these libraries.
Example: TXT
 from pathlib import Path
text = Path("documents/manual.txt").read_text(
encoding="utf-8"
)
Example: PDF
 import fitz # PyMuPDF
pdf = fitz.open("documents/manual.pdf")
for page_number, page in enumerate(pdf, start=1):
text = page.get_text()
print(page_number, text[:200])
The key design principle is: all supported file types should eventually become text plus metadata.

3. Clean and Normalize Text
Extracted text may contain extra spaces, repeated line breaks, headers, footers, or formatting artifacts. Clean only what is

4. Split Text into Chunks
An embedding model and vector store work better when a large document is divided into smaller meaningful pieces.

A common beginner strategy is recursive text splitting with a chunk size and overlap. Start with a reasonable value and
tune it based on retrieval quality; there is no universal best chunk size.
Why overlap?
If a sentence or concept crosses a chunk boundary, overlap gives the next chunk some surrounding context.

 def index_file(file_path):
documents = load_file(file_path)
documents = clean(documents)
chunks = split_into_chunks(documents)
vectors = embed(chunks)
vector_store.add(
vectors=vectors,
texts=chunks,
metadata=metadata
)
vector_store.persist()

so the rest of the RAG application stays portable.

If retrieval returns the wrong chunk, debug retrieval first. If retrieval is correct but the answer is poor, investigate the
prompt, context size, model, or generation settings.

24. Security Notes
Use a non-confidential test document first. Before sending DSP documentation or sensitive telecom information to an

external API, follow your organization's security and data-handling requirements. Never hard-code API keys or commit
secret files. In production, authorization must determine which documents a user can retrieve; the LLM should not enforce
access control.
